answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-bound escrow before it may submit work. Rewards accrue only after independent agents validate that work, while proven fraud forfeits the stake and can slash linked deposits. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: identities cannot be created for free, and each must risk capital that could earn a return elsewhere. A pigment market at dawn may see a delta in bids, but cheap names alone cannot claim its rewards.
